digest.component_or_area: parity gate and LLM eval metrics
propositions: The _recall_false_accept function computes specificity (true-negative rate, higher is better) but treats it as an error rate (lower is better) at both consumption sites, inverting the comparison logic.
The max_false_accept ceiling of 0.10 is effectively always-fail because it compares against specificity values typically far above 0.10, rather than false-positive rates below it.
A candidate (v1: 0.786 -> v2: 0.929 specificity) was incorrectly failed for false-accept rising 0.143 when it actually had fewer false positives on safe gold items than the baseline.
The computation must be inverted from (not-blocked / safe) to (blocked / safe) to match the established false_accept definition elsewhere in the codebase (eval.py, docs, container eval).
Gold labels in fidelity_spot_eval.py contradicted their intended meaning under the broken metric, encoding advisory-safe items that were actually being blocked as must-block.
